text:
Clayton Keller has turned into Utah's distributor in chief. Twenty-two of his 27 points are assists, and 17 have come on the power play, which tells you where the Mammoth's offense runs right now: through the captain's stick, with the man advantage. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists last season, so none of this is new in kind, only in degree.

The goals are the odd part. He has one in his last ten games and is shooting 9.1%, below the 12% our numbers treat as his true level, on chances that look like his usual ones. That gap tends to close. The thing worth watching is at five on five, where Utah's share of expected goals (the quality of chances) is about seven and a half points lower with him on the ice than without him. For a player Evolving-Hockey rated sixth among all forwards last season, that's the number we'd want to see move, especially with the Mammoth coming off three straight overtime losses.
